Refer to “Buoyancy Control” section for the minimum negative buoyancy requirements. Minimum depth of cover in wetlands will be three (3) feet if conventionally laid, and 15 feet when bored. Buoyancy control shall be used when the pipeline crosses through the following wetland areas: • Wetlands typically containing saturated soils or standing water. • Dry wetlands (usually no standing water or saturated soil) with soils that are not dense enough when saturated to resist the buoyant force of the pipe. At conventional lay waterbody crossing locations the depth of cover shall be 5-feet below the lowest existing section of the crossing. Where concrete coating or weights are applied, the depth of cover shall be measured from the top of pipe to the lowest point on the river bottom or streambed. The HDD method is proposed for all major watercourses for this project. 6.8 HYDROSTATIC TESTING Hydrostatic testing will follow the requirements of 49 CFR 195, Subpart E ‐ Pressure Testing and ASME B31.4. Above ground and shop fabricated piping shall be tested to the pressure designated on the included piping specifications for a minimum of four (4) hours. Below ground piping shall be tested for a minimum of eight (8) hours. Pipe sections welded together for HDD installation will be hydrostatically tested for a minimum of one (1) hour prior to the pull‐back operation to ensure the line segment meets all integrity requirements. A Hydrostatic Test Plan will be developed to define the test limits (which account for elevation differences), pressures, and procedures for each test segment. The testing pressures for the mainline will be at least 1.25 times the maximum design pressure. The maximum testing pressure at any point in the test section will be limited to the pressure that produces the hoop stress equal to 100% SMYS of pipe material.
